seo.description: The Portuguese Cistern in El Jadida — vaulted underground hall, columns and water reflections. UNESCO gem of the Portuguese City.
seo.og_description: Manueline underground hall with columns reflecting in the water — the most photographed site in El Jadida.

name: Portuguese Cistern
hero_subtitle: Vaulted underground hall and zenithal light — the jewel of the Portuguese City.

overview.title: The underground jewel of El Jadida
overview.p1: Built in the 16th century by the Portuguese, first as a warehouse or arsenal and later converted into a cistern, this 34 × 34 m hall rests on 25 columns supporting Manueline vaults. A thin layer of water reflects the arches and the light streaming from the central oculus.
overview.p2: The setting was used as a filming location for Orson Welles's Othello. The atmosphere is unique: silence, reflections and interplay of shadows. Visit preferably in the morning to enjoy the natural light.
overview.p3: It is the most iconic site in El Jadida and a must-see during any visit to the citadel.

1.title: Best light
1.desc: The sunbeam through the oculus is at its sharpest.

3.title: Soft atmosphere
3.desc: Fewer visitors late in the day.

food.title: Eating around the harbor (Portuguese Cistern)
food.p1: The fishing harbor area is one of the easiest spots in El Jadida to find fresh seafood right after spending time around Portuguese Cistern.
food.li1: Grilled fish plates and seafood spots along the quay and adjacent streets.
food.li2: Casual cafés for mint tea or morning coffee watching harbor life.
food.li3: Neighborhood eateries near the Portuguese City and Place Mohammed V within a short walk.
food.li4: Keep food covered or indoors—seabirds around the piers are quick to swoop in.
food.li5: Bring drinking water and sun or wind protection when walking along the docks.
food.p2: MAD cash is practical for small harbor stalls and casual cafés.

tips.title: Practical tips for the Portuguese Cistern

1.title: Opening hours
1.desc: Check daily hours; often closed on Tuesdays. Arrive early for the light.

2.title: Photos
2.desc: Wet floor: watch out for reflections. Tripod helpful if permitted.

3.title: Respect
3.desc: Do not touch the water or columns; stay on permitted areas.

q1.question: How much time should I plan for the cistern?
q1.answer: 30 to 45 minutes is plenty for the visit and photos.

q2.question: Is there water on the floor?
q2.answer: Yes, a thin layer of water creates the famous reflections. Wear suitable footwear.

q3.question: Can I visit with children?
q3.answer: Yes, the site is accessible; watch steps and wet surfaces.

q4.question: Is the cistern open every day?
q4.answer: Often closed on Tuesdays. Check local hours before heading out.

q5.question: Do I need a guide?
q5.answer: Not mandatory, though a guide enriches the historical visit of the citadel.
